title: UEFA Votes Unanimous Boycott of FIFA Competitions Over Private Equity Plan
dek: All 55 UEFA member associations voted unanimously on July 30 to boycott all FIFA tournaments if FIFA president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell a stake in World Cup revenue to private investors proceeds. The boycott threat targets a proposal to raise $20 billion through the sale of roughly 20 percent of FIFA Forward Enterprises, backed by investor Josh Kushner and JP Morgan, with a Sept. 19 deadline set for approval.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: UEFA's 55 member associations, including Germany, France, England, and world champions Spain, voted unanimously on July 30 to boycott all FIFA competitions unless Infantino's private equity proposal is abandoned entirely.
bottom_line: The Sept. 19 deadline becomes the pressure point: whether UEFA's unanimity holds and whether other continental confederations align with Europe or fracture over the $80+ million payouts each association stands to lose. If Infantino proceeds and Europe walks, world football enters uncharted legal and structural territory; if he backs down, the precedent shifts power sharply toward confederation governance. Watch for statements from CONCACAF, CONMEBOL, AFC, and CAF in the coming weeks.
body: All 55 UEFA member associations voted unanimously on July 30 to boycott all FIFA competitions if FIFA president Gianni Infantino's private equity plan moves forward. The coordinated action by Europe's largest football confederation weaponizes the sport's most valuable asset, the World Cup, as leverage against what UEFA frames as the privatization of football governance.

UEFA held an emergency virtual meeting on July 30 with all 55 member associations present. According to ESPN's reporting, over 50 associations took the floor and expressed unanimity in opposition to Infantino's proposals. The confederation resolved to boycott all FIFA tournaments unless the private equity proposal is abandoned entirely and binding assurances are given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

The plan at issue involves the sale of roughly 20 percent of FIFA Forward Enterprises (FFE), a consolidated entity controlling several of FIFA's money-making operations, to a private equity consortium. According to Front Office Sports, the lead investor is Thrive Eternal, run by Joshua Kushner. The proposed deal, backed by JP Morgan, would raise approximately $20 billion and trigger payouts of over $80 million to each of FIFA's 211 member associations between now and 2037. The private equity stake would give outside investors influence over future World Cups, including broadcasting and commercial deals tied to the tournament.

Major nations including Germany, France, England, and world champions Spain would not participate in the men's or women's World Cup if UEFA implements the boycott, per ESPN's reporting. The first test of the threat will come in September when Poland is due to host the Women's U-20 World Cup. UEFA further cited the lack of meaningful consultation over the FIFA plans as a governance failure by the world governing body.

Infantino set a Sept. 19 deadline for associations to accept the plan. FIFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment, per Front Office Sports. The sources do not record any formal statement from FIFA defending the process or the merits of the proposal; FIFA's rationale and response remain absent from the record.

UEFA has made similar threats in the past. According to Front Office Sports, the confederation previously threatened a World Cup boycott when FIFA proposed holding the tournament every two years. The sources do not assess whether the follow-through risk and credibility of that prior threat shed light on UEFA's willingness to enforce this one.
